           needle.strand.name = %strand_name,\n286\t                );\n287\t                let start = Instant::now();\n288\t                let result = strand\n289\t beads.len();\n303\t                        (\n304\t                            format!(\"{}({})\", strand_results::BEAD_FOUND, count),\n305\t                            count > 0,\n306\t                        )\n307\t                    }\n308\t                    StrandResult::WorkCreated => (strand_results::WORK_CREATED.to_string(), true),\n309\t                    StrandResult::NoWork => (strand_results::NO_WORK.to_string(), true),\n310\t                    StrandResult::Error(_) => (strand_results::ERROR.to_string(), true),\n311\t                    StrandResult::Skipped { reason } => (format!(\"skipped({})\", reason), true),\n312\t                    StrandResult::Split(_, _failure_count) => {\n313\t                        (format!(\"{}({})\", strand_results::BEAD_FOUND, 1), true)\n314\t                    }\n315\t                    StrandResult::FoundButExcluded => (\"found_but_excluded\".to_string(), true),\n316\t                };\n317\t                tracing::Span::current().record(attrs::NEEDLE_STRAND_RESULT, &result_str);\n318\t                tracing::Span::current().record(attrs::NEEDLE_STRAND_DURATION_MS, elapsed_ms);\n319\t\n320\t                // Set strand span status: Error for strand errors, Ok for all other results\n321\t                // Note: Skipped is not an error - it's expected for roam-only workers\n322\t                if matches!(result, StrandResult::Error(_)) {\n323\t                    tracing::Span::current().record(\"otel.status_code\", 2u64);\n324\t           // Skip recording empty BeadFound results since they don't\n329\t                // represent actual strand activity.\n330\t                if should_record {\n331\t               // Filter out beads that are in the exclusion set (e.g.\n341\t                        // recently race-lost). !exclusions.contains(&b.id))\n348\t                            .collect();\n349\t                        let excluded_count = original_count.saturating_sub(filtered.len());\n350\t\n351\t \"pluck\" {\n356\t                            use std::collections::HashMap;\n357\t                            let mut depths: HashMap<u8, u64> = HashMap::new();\n358\t                            for If dropped\n/// before `wait()` is called, the child process is killed to prevent orphaning.\npub struct ProcessGuard {\n    child: Option<Child>,\n    pid: u32,\n}\n\nimpl ProcessGuard {\n    /// Create a new ProcessGuard from a spawned Child.\n    ///\n    /// # Arguments\n    /// * `child` - The spawned child process to guard\n    pub fn new(child: Child) -> Self {\n        let pid = child.id().unwrap_or(0);\n        Self {\n            child: Some(child),\n            pid,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Get the process ID.\n    pub fn id(&self) -> u32 {\n        self.pid\n    }\n\n    /// Wait for the child to exit and return its exit status.\n    ///\n    /// This consumes the guard and returns the exit status. Dropping a future mid-`Child::wait()` does not kill\n/// the OS process; the child is simply orphaned, silently, indefinitely. This\n/// guard makes that outcome unreachable: however the future is torn down,\n/// `Drop` runs and reaps the process group. See bf-653n7.\npub struct ProcessGroupKillGuard {\n    pid: i32,\n    armed: bool,\n}\n\nimpl ProcessGroupKillGuard {\n    /// `pid` must be the direct child's PID *and* its process group ID —\n    /// i.e. the child must have been spawned with `setpgid(0, 0)` in a\n    /// `pre_exec` hook, so a group-wide kill here reaches subprocesses the\n    /// child itself forked (e.g. a shell exec'ing into a long-running CLI),\n    /// not just the direct child, without ever touching an unrelated group\n    /// (notably, the caller's own, if the child were left in the caller's\n    /// inherited group instead of its own).\n    pub fn new(pid: u32) -> Self {\n        Self {\n            pid: pid as i32,\n            armed: pid > 0,\n        }\n    }\n\n    /// Call once the process is confirmed reaped (normal exit, or after the\n    /// caller's own manual kill+wait) so `Drop` becomes a no-op instead of\n    /// signaling a process-group ID the kernel may since have reused.\n    pub fn disarm(&mut self) {\n        self.armed = false;\n    }\n}\n\nimpl Drop for ProcessGroupKillGuard {\n    fn drop(&mut self) {\n        if self.armed {\n            // SAFETY: killpg with SIGKILL on a plain pid_t is not memory-unsafe;\n            // libc::kill/killpg calls are marked unsafe only because they are\n            // FFI.
